covers: Europe Thu 26 Nov session (closing figures not confirmed; intraday levels only)

developments.text: The US proposed new tariffs on 14 trading partners including China, the EU, Japan and India, mostly 15–20% and up to 35% for Vietnam; officials say they are months from taking effect and lower rates are on offer for trade deals.
developments.title: US Section 301 'overcapacity' tariffs

developments.text: The regional tech index bounced 2.5% after losing about 12% this month on AI-bubble worries.
developments.title: European tech rebound

for_malaysia: Trade channel: the EU faces a proposed 15% US tariff, which weighs on European demand for Malaysian electronics and palm-oil-linked goods if it sticks. In the near term, Europe's tech rebound helps the global chip mood that Bursa's semiconductor names follow.
gaps: Stoxx 600, DAX and FTSE 100 closing levels not confirmed (Reuters and FT unreachable).
GBP/USD, Bund 10Y, Gilt 10Y, ECB deposit rate and BoE Bank Rate not confirmed this run.
headline: European stocks rallied about 1.6–1.7%, led by chipmakers, as investors shrugged off new US tariffs.
numbers_note: The Stoxx 600's roughly 1.6% intraday gain and the DAX's 1.9% passed the stock filter, but these are midday readings and the closes were not confirmed.

points.text: The Stoxx 600 was about 1.6% higher at 635.80 by midday London time, with all sectors and major bourses positive; the DAX led with a 1.9% rise and the Stoxx tech index jumped 2.5% after losing about 12% this month.
Bloomberg reported the Stoxx 600 rallying 1.7% as Wednesday's late US dip-buying pulled the Nasdaq 100 back from the brink of a bear market.
AJ Bell's Russ Mould said the new US tariffs were not as bad as feared but warned against complacency, pointing to oil prices and possible retaliation.
The ECB's account of its October meeting said financial conditions had tightened on a repricing of risk, though the October PMIs still signalled expansion.
